result.rationale: The migration inserts old embeddable_hosts values verbatim via raw SQL ('#{h}'), bypassing EmbeddableHost's before_validation normalization (self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')). Meanwhile the removed SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? stripped protocols before comparing, and old data could include http:// prefixes (the old code handled them, and the diff's own spec fabricates a host with 'http://discourse.org'). After migration, record_for_host compares lower(host) = uri.host ('discourse.org') against stored 'http://discourse.org', which never matches, so previously allowed hosts get InvalidA

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration reads the old SiteSetting 'embeddable_hosts' value and does a raw SQL INSERT of each line as the `host` column (VALUES ('#{h}', ...)) without running the EmbeddableHost model’s `before_validation` normalization that strips `http(s)://` and paths (app/models/embeddable_host.rb). After the change, host checks use `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` / `host_allowed?` which compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)` (hostname only). If a previously-working entry was stored as `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234` (explicitly supported by the old SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? implementation that parsed URIs), it would be migrated verbatim and then fail to match `uri.host`, causing embeds to be rejected with InvalidAccess.
